utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Madam Registrar, will you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is the case number IT-99-36-A, the Prosecutor versus Radoslav Brdjanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Brdjanin, I would like to make sure that you can understand and hear the proceedings in a language that you are familiar with. Mr. Brdjanin.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Microphone, Mr. Brdjanin, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon to everyone. I can follow in a language I can understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... could I now have -- please have the appearances for the parties. The Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. BRADY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Helen Brady appearing on behalf of the Prosecution, together with Katharina Margetts, and our case manager Ms. Lourdes Galicia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Brady. I understand that Mr. Ackerman, counsel for the Defence, is supposed to be appearing by telephone. The Registrar, is Mr. Ackerman on the line?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Would you please inform the Court whether the Registry has had any contact with Mr. Ackerman today.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. We did not have any contact with Mr. Ackerman today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Could you kindly confirm for the record that the order scheduling the Status Conference was sent to Mr. Ackerman?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. It's been sent to Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Registrar. Unfortunately, Mr. Ackerman's absence somewhat limits what we can do today. Mr. Brdjanin, it appears that your counsel is not on the line. I want to give you the option of whether to proceed or not in light of Mr. Ackerman's absence. If you decide to proceed, I will only ask you questions about your mental or physical health. We will not discuss any other issue relevant to the appeals in this case. So I will ask you, Mr. Brdjanin, whether you wish to proceed, and be asked about your mental and physical health; or would you prefer to adjourn this Status Conference and reconvene it when Mr. Ackerman is present or on the phone? Before you answer, which channel am I supposed to be on?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Number 4. Yeah. You may proceed, Mr. Brdjanin.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We may continue, Your Honour, as far as I'm concerned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, Mr. Brdjanin. Let me then ask you whether you have any concerns regarding your physical or mental well-being.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As concerns my well-being, I have no issues to raise. I can only say that it is as old as I am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Brdjanin. You may be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I inquire something about the appeal itself?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: We are working on it, Mr. Brdjanin, and we will -- we will try to schedule the hearing as soon as we can. I can assure you that we are working hard on your case. Any other questions, Mr. Brdjanin?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't have in mind the case in its entirety. I just wanted to see whether I could be given the appeal in my own language, in a language I can understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: I will check into the status of translations and we will let you know where we are standing, we are on that. Okay?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you. So, again, because of the situation that has arisen, I have avoided going into any questions pertaining to the respective appeals. And I will not do that now. We will wait and deal with other issues, namely the issues pertaining to the appeals when the Defence counsel is with us. Unfortunately, it is unlikely that we will be able to have a conference dealing with these issues 120 days of our 1 March 2006 Status Conference. I want to note for the record that the Appeals Chamber scheduled a Status Conference within 120 days of the last Status Conference, and that our inability today to let the parties raise all issues normally raised at a Status Conference is due to the fact that Defence counsel did not appear today, either in person or on the phone. That said, I thank the Prosecution, and I thank Mr. Brdjanin for their attendance today, and I call the proceedings to a close. Thank you very much.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 5.44 p.m.
